definition: The start of a frame is its frame top.
note: Heavily used far from its definition; g-frame's text only mentions frame tops in passing. Draft: the start of a frame, the instant a drain applies staged writes and root inputs change. A sense of g-frame is the alternative.

definition: At each step boundary the framework runs the boundary sequence. It integrates, projects, runs the boundary sweep (...), evaluates all guards once against that sweep, and fires the eligible events.
note: Defined in §5.3 and cited from execution chapters; g-frame and g-projection use it without an entry. Draft: integrate, project, iterate sweep-guards-handlers to quiescence, run due updates, publish.

definition: every event round (one pass of sweep, guard checks and handlers) before the last
note: The literal phrase is rare, but the bare 'round' of the iteration recurs about 30 times, 14 in §10.6, defined in §2.3:451 and §2.4:525. Draft: one pass of sweep, guard checks and handlers inside a boundary's iteration to quiescence.

definition: The hand-down is the component's own stage-1 ports.
note: Used in §9.3 and §13.8 away from its definition. Draft: the component's own stage-1 return, delivered as y_x or y_s in the stage-2 bundle.

definition: The fused idiom stands. Compute each law once, in a stage. Publish it. Let x_deriv/s_update copy from y.
note: Used in §7.4 and §14.7 away from §5.3. Draft: compute each law once in an output stage, publish it as a port, and let x_deriv or s_update copy it from y.

definition: A hop runs through one member, a component on the cycle, from the face that one wire enters to the port the next wire leaves. The hop holds iff that member's stage-2 function routes the face to the port.
note: Defined in §5.4 and used about 11 times in §13.8; g-algebraic-loop's entry does not define it. Draft: a step through one cycle member from the face a wire enters to the port the next wire leaves; dead if stage 2 does not route them.

definition: The second is the walk clause, for a continuous consumer only. A walking producer leaf (...) requires an unpinned entry.
note: Defined in §6.1 and used five times in §8.2 and in §13.7; no entry. Draft: the wire type-check that a walking producer leaf needs an unpinned consumer entry; a pinned leaf satisfies either.

definition: The walk stops at an immutable type that is not isbits and treats it as one opaque leaf.
note: Used far from §4.3, six times in §8.2; the glossary has no entry (g-leaf-walk and g-field-handle do not define it). Draft: an immutable non-isbits value the leaf walk stores whole as one leaf, such as a field handle or a Symbol.

definition: Every connection endpoint names an immediate child and one of its faces. The one-level rule covers all three wiring declarations.
note: Also spelled one-level routing; used in §8.8 and §13.3 away from §6.1. Draft: every wire endpoint names an immediate child and one of its faces; routing across levels is declared level by level.

definition: Routing across several levels is therefore declared level by level, with each assembly speaking only of its own children. This restriction is named the locality law.
note: Bucket D term whose use has grown to seven, five of them in chapters 13 and 14. Draft: an assembly speaks only of its own children, and fragments of the condition algebra follow it as guidance.

definition: authors should bundle what shares a stage and is consumed together; data written by different external writers, or at different cadences, must not share a port
note: Two named rules that compose into one principle (§4.3:954); each is cited from §8.3 or §8.8. Draft: bundle what shares a stage and is read together; never share a port between writers or cadences.

definition: An entry of any of the three is a wire, and an entry of the first is a local wire.
note: Known gap. A sense of entry: one element of local_wires, input_wires or output_wires; the text does not use the bare phrase wiring entry in chapters 1-7 beyond §6.1.

definition: Scatter/gather is the whole protocol. (...) The framework scatters each field into that port's concretely typed cell. Every reader gathers views from cells.
note: Named protocol in §4.3, but many hits are the ordinary verb in other chapters; the orchestrator should decide whether §4.3 alone needs a gloss. Draft: the framework scatters a stage's returned fields into typed cells; readers gather views from cells.

definition: A strapdown inertial measurement unit (IMU) integrates over each sample interval and zeroes its integrals at every sample.
note: Defined in §3.4 and worked in §8.6 (uncited at one use in §3.3). Draft: the IMU pattern of integrating over a sample interval and zeroing at each sample, the hardest case for the two-leaf split.

definition: A run starts at its origin t₀
note: Plain English plus a symbol; g-boundary-zero and g-checkpoint cover its role, so a gloss at §2.1 suffices.

definition: An output stage returns its port NamedTuple, y, and nothing else
note: Sibling of the handler return law; a sub-heading in §5.2 and one use, cited by section like the handler return law.

definition: the gate idiom for localizing mixed predicates
note: Two uses, defined in §10.4.

definition: the signal requirement is immutability plus frozen references
note: Both uses in §4.1.

definition: Pre-sampling is an idiom built on top
note: Both uses in §4.4.

definition: Field-addressed staging is a recorded guarded addition
note: Single uses; each is a guarded addition and already glossed inline.

definition: Fold order is author-visible. It is the positional order of the junction's inputs.
note: Used in §6.2 and the g-summing-junction entry, which states it.

definition: The zero-contributor spelling is a library Constant source
note: Defined and used in §6.2; g-constant-source covers the mechanism.

definition: Scheduled gains are inputs; A commanded reset of a discrete component is a same-tick input, consumed in the output stage
note: All uses sit in §5.3.

definition: three-level funnel (stage name at its tier ⊇ bundle ⊇ reads)
note: One use.

definition: An end time stops the run at the first grid boundary at or after it.
note: All uses sit in §2.4 and §12.4; named by stop request and stop word entries.

definition: The deployment parameters are the step h, the base tick period, the integration method, the localization tolerance and budget, and the firing budget
note: Three uses; g-deployment covers the artifact.

definition: port-level acyclic yet admit no evaluation order
note: Bold-defined inside the algebraic loop entry, which also contains the remedy ladder and the two other rungs (3 uses of remedy ladder).

definition: The remedy ladder for artificial loops has three rungs
note: Described inside the g-algebraic-loop entry; link there.

definition: the framework-owned home of one of a component's state letters, x, s or m
note: Alias of the letters entry.

definition: y_state is stage 1 and y_direct is stage 2.
note: Alias of the stage function entry.

definition: A junction is an ordinary stateless component with N inputs of one type, in1 to inN, and one output, out.
note: The generic junction is described by the summing junction entry.

definition: state views (zero-copy reconstructions of the component's stores)
note: Alias of the view entry.
